newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress wants stable government.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress wants stable government.

text.p: India's Congress party, which provides crucial support to the ruling United Front coalition, said on Friday it wants a stable government and has a "sweet" relationship with the coalition.

Newly-elected Congress president Sitaram Kesri told a news conference the party was committed to a stable relationship with the United Front until Congress had a chance to form a new government after fresh general elections.
Asked about the United Front, Kesri said: "Our relations are sweet and will remain sweet. And when the mandate of the country is for a coalition, we will obey it.
"It is wrong to interpret that we will withdraw our support to the government. That will continue for a good number of days," Kesri said.

Congress in March withdrew its vital backing to then prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government and later helped to topple him in a parliamentary confidence vote. It resumed support to the coalition only after it agreed to replace Deve Gowda.
"We withdrew support on March 30 due to certain occurrences," Kesri said without elaborating.
"Their behaviour is now better than it was earlier. Therefore, Congress wants to continue its support, and the United Front should also see that it takes care of Congress interests."
Kesri was elected Congress president for a second term on Thursday, winning more than 6,000 votes in a three-man race. His closest opponent won less than 900 of the 7,557 votes polled.

After his election, the shrewd 76-year-old leader said his overwhelming victory vindicated his decision to topple Deve Gowda. The shock move had plunged India into weeks of political turmoil and drew sharp criticism from Kesri's detractors.

At Friday's news conference, Kesri said: "The question of Congress forming a government arises only if there are elections in the next one or two years, and if Congress is successful in those elections, only then can it form the government."
"Till then, our commitment with the United Front remains and we want that the government remains stable," he added.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 15-party coalition leans heavily on Congress support for its survival. Congress's 140 deputies shore up the United Front's 179 lawmakers in the 543-member lower house of parliament.
